en: Then, having risen in the morning and reflected, "I shall again make the world free from obstacles so that it may reach the state of the Vajra-holder," one should instantly, following emptiness, visualize a sun disk in front by means of the syllable *repha*. Upon that sun, one should visualize a *viśvavajra* marked with the syllable *haṃ* (or *hūṃ*), and by means of that very *vajra*, one should visualize a rampart and a cage-binding.

Having thus visualized the Vajrapañjara and other [protective enclosures], one who possesses the yoga of the Lord of the Maṇḍala himself should, from within its center, draw in the obstructors of the ten directions with rays of light emanating from the syllable *hūṃ* residing in his heart, and deliver them over to the ten Wrathful Deities projected from that *hūṃ*.
—From the *Ḍākinīvajrapañjara* (The Vajrapañjara of the Ḍākinīs)

Then, having risen early, one should contemplate: "In order to establish myself in the state of Vajradhara, I shall once again eliminate all obstacles. Following that emptiness, in an instant, one visualizes a sun disk as the preliminary support; from that sun arises a *hūṃ*, which becomes a crossed vajra (*viśvavajra*). From that very vajra arise the enclosure walls and—

"Furthermore, one should meditate on the binding of the neck" means that one meditates on the vajra-fence and so forth; within that, being endowed with the yoga of oneself as the Lord of the Mandala, one should summon all obstructors from the ten directions with light rays emanated from the syllable *hūṃ* abiding in the heart, and entrust them to the ten wrathful deities emanated from that same syllable *hūṃ*.
And those *krodha* [deities], eighteen, twelve, or eight *aṅgulas* in length respectively, measuring six, four, or two-and-a-half *aṅgulas* [in width], are made of khadira wood, bone, or iron.

Having visualized ten stakes—placed in nine vessels, smeared with white mustard seeds and red sandalwood paste, bound with five-colored threads, worshipped, and adorned with garlands of red flowers by means of the three-syllable mantra—one should grasp them below the navel in the form of a single-pointed spike. Above that, one’s own form as a wrathful deity, blazing like the fire at the end of an aeon, takes up with the left vajra-fist and holds with the right hand a mallet, which has been transformed from the primary attribute and is bound with a garland of red flowers.

Having caused the ten vighnas, beginning with Indra, together with their retinues, to enter the ten wells of the syllable *hūṃ* uttered with a long sound, one should nail them to the head with this mantra. Those wrathful deities are eighteen, twelve, or eight finger-breadths in length respectively, and six finger-breadths in width.

The fourth and third [of these] are stakes made of khadira wood, bone, or iron; they are consecrated in a new vessel, smeared with white mustard seeds and white sandalwood, wrapped with threads of five colors, properly worshipped, and empowered with the three syllables. These ten stakes, bound with garlands of red flowers, are placed at the navel.

Visualize yourself with a sharp, one-pointed form below and, above, your own reflection in the form of a wrathful deity blazing like the fire at the end of an aeon; then, grasping [the vajra] with the left hand in a vajra-fist and holding with the right hand a vajra-staff—the primary emblem having been completely transformed—adorned with a garland of red flowers.

From the long-syllabled *hūṃ*, ten wells arise; one should cause the ten obstacles, such as the sense faculties and so forth, together with their retinues, to enter them, and then strike them at the crown of the head with a ritual stake (*kīla*).

Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Yamāntakṛt, nail-pierce all the wicked Indras and Upendras together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Prajñāntakṛt, nail-pierce all the wicked Yamas together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Padmāntakṛt, nail-pierce all the wicked Nāgas together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Vighnāntakṛt, nail down all malevolent Kuveras together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Acala, nail down all malevolent Īśānas together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Ṭakkirāja, nail down all malevolent Agnis together with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ!

Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Nīladaṇḍa, nail the entire host of wicked Nairṛtis along with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Mahābala, nail the entire host of wicked Vāyus along with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ! Oṃ āḥ hūṃ!
Uṣṇīṣacakravartin, nail the entire host of wicked Ārka, Candra, and Pitāmaha along with their retinues! Hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ āḥ hūṃ! Sumbha! All you wicked Vemacitrin and earth deities, together with your retinues, be impaled! Hūṃ phaṭ!

The mantra is as follows: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ YAMĀNTAKṚTA SARVADUṢṬĀN AINDRĀN AUPENDRĀN SA-PARIVĀRĀN KĪLAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ | OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ PRAJÑĀNTAKṚTA SARVADUṢṬĀN YĀMYĀN SA-PARIVĀRĀN KĪLAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ | OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ PADMĀNTAKṚTA SARVADUṢṬĀN NĀGĀN SA-PARIVĀRĀN KĪLAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ ||

oṃ āḥ hūṃ vighnāntakṛt sarvaduṣṭakuberāṇāṃ saparivārāṇāṃ kilaya hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ āḥ hūṃ acala sarvaduṣṭāśanānāṃ saparivārāṇāṃ kilaya hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ āḥ hūṃ ṭakkirāja sarvaduṣṭāgnīnāṃ saparivārāṇāṃ kilaya hūṃ phaṭ |

oṃ āḥ hūṃ nīladaṇḍa sarvaduṣṭanirghātanāparivāraṇakīlaya hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ āḥ hūṃ mahābala sarvaduṣṭabhayasanparivāraṇakīlaya hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ āḥ hūṃ uṣṇīṣacakravartin sarvaduṣṭārkatandrapatimahānasaparivāraṇakīlaya hūṃ phaṭ | oṃ āḥ |

With these mantras—*HŪṂ SUMBHARĀJA SARVADUṢṬĀN VAICITRAPRITHIVĪDEVA-TĀŚAPARIVĀRAṆAKĪLAYA HŪṂ PHAṬ*—the Ācārya should perform the ritual of driving in and hammering the stakes upon ten mounds of clay outside the maṇḍala house in the directions starting from the east. [In case of inability, then the Door-Masters (dvārācāryas) should do so: he should drive in a stake to the east of the eastern stake of Uṣṇīṣa, and to the west of the western stake of Sumbha.

With these mantras, the preceptor should cast and strike lumps of clay in the ten directions outside the mandala pavilion; if he is unable to do so, the gate preceptors should do so. For the *Uṣṇīṣa*, one should cast and strike east of the eastern stake, and for the *Ghantakara*, one should cast and strike west of the western stake.

One should honor the wrathful deities in the form of stakes with parasols, banners, flags, and so forth; and one should worship them daily at the three junctions of the day with offerings of bali, food, flowers, incense, and the like. ||o||

One should please the wrathful deities of the *kīla* effigies with parasols, victory banners, streamers, and so forth; and on each day, during the three sessions, one should worship them with *bali* offerings, incense, music, flowers, fragrant incense, and the like.

Alternatively, even without stakes made of khadira wood or other materials, while meditating as prescribed, one should perform the ritual of piercing and striking; then, turning with palms upturned and reciting "Oṃ Vajra Hūṃ," one should split the earth and resolve that it is thus free from obstacles.

Alternatively, even if stakes made of *khadira* wood or the like are unavailable, one should perform the driving and striking of the stake through meditation alone as previously described. Having rotated the hand so that it rests in the posture of a sandal (*paryaṅka*), one should strike the ground against the obstructors while reciting "Oṃ vajra hūṃ," and thus form a firm resolve.
This is the procedure for the ritual of the obstacle-stake (*vighnakīlanavidhi*). || o ||
Thus concludes the ritual for striking the obstacles with the ritual stake.
